label: adult-s0
summary: This network predicts the probability of the low-income class (income of at most $50k) on the adult census data as a sigmoid of a mostly linear score. Its linear part carries most of the ranking (training AUC 0.906 with it, 0.743 with it switched off); its largest direct weights, for capital gain, being a husband, years of education, being a wife, age and hours worked, lower the predicted probability. Nine hidden parts add group-specific shifts. A gate open for the 12959 women and for the 12 men in private household service raises it (on average 0.62 logit for women). Wives, executives and managers, and people with a capital gain above a threshold between 4300 US dollars and 4350 US dollars get further decreases beyond their direct edges. Missing work class, separation and work without pay (fitted to 17 rows) get increases. A unit for people born in Japan cancels most of the direct Japan edge, and one unit is dead. Switching the nine hidden parts off together changes training AUC from 0.9056 to 0.9025.
